page.layout: One page of text, single column; a verse block in italic between the running text and the heading PYTHAGORAS; a drop-cap verse, a heading XENOPHON with following verse. Page number top right. Running head at top centre.

main_text.p: ius,vt à Lutheranis, quos vocabant, e- uersæ fragmenta,boni sacrifici sangui- ne asperserant, vt hac miraculi specie Regem aduersus illos magis ac magis incenderent.

p.i: Axea quæ fuerat nunc est argentea Virgo,

l.i: ed quàm prædones contra,non possit imago
ferrea concludunt illam quæ claustra quibusuis
Vne igitur perges motu sensuque carentem
At,tu Rex,potius nobis hæc secula mutans,

main_text.head: PYTHAGORAS.
XENOPHON, læua calamum, dex- tra gladium gestans.

p.i: Vid Marti & Musis, Xenophon? Sic Vici- mus olim Barbariem gladio, barbariem calamo.

page.notes: Printed page with a decorative woodcut-style ornament border; the verse opening lines in the first stanza are partly damaged. Several words in the verse are doubtful, notably "Axea", "ferrea", and "Vne"; the initial letters of "Audent" and "Virtutem" are decorative drop caps. The "L" and "O" are decorative initials.
